explanation: The word is German for 'compulsion to move'. Because a player may not pass in chess, being in zugzwang can lose a game that standing still would have saved.

claims.text: In chess, zugzwang is a position in which any move the player to move makes worsens their position.
A zwischenzug is an in-between move, a fianchetto develops a bishop on a long diagonal, and en prise describes a piece left open to capture.
Zugzwang is German for 'compulsion to move'.
Passing is not allowed in chess, so a player in zugzwang must still make a move.
